segments.text: Here's a question.
Where does the purpose in your work come from?
Does the job give it to you?
Your manager?
The company?
A lot of people live as though it does.
When the work is interesting, I'll be interested.
When someone motivates me, I'll be motivated.
But what if we've got that backwards?
What if the job doesn't have to give you purpose?
What if you bring the purpose?
You bring the meaning.
You bring the intention.
You bring the energy.
And when you understand that, you stop waiting for your circumstances to determine the kind
of day you're going to have.
You start creating it.
Imagine two people arriving for exactly the same shift, same workplace, same hours, same
responsibilities.
One thinks, here we go again.
I'll get through the day, get paid, and go home.
And of course, money matters.
We all have responsibilities.
But the other arrives thinking, I'm going to make today count.
I'm going to learn.
I'm going to serve people well.
I'm going to bring great energy to my team.
And if faith is important to them, perhaps, through the way I work today, I can serve
God.
Same job.
Completely different experience.
One is waiting for the day to give them something.
The other has decided what they're going to bring to the day.
And you're going to spend thousands of hours of your life working.
Why just get through them?
Use those hours to become more confident, more skilled, more resilient, a better teammate,
someone people trust.
If you're going to spend the hours anyway, why not use them to become someone you're
proud of?
We call this your governing intention.
It's the deeper intention underneath the way you approach your day.
It could be get through the day or make the day count.
Same eight hours.
But repeated over time, those intentions can create very different people.
Your intention influences your choices.
Your choices, repeated, become habits.
Your habits shape your character.
Eventually, you don't have to remind yourself to bring purpose.
You become a purposeful person, someone who cares.
Someone who notices.
Someone who takes responsibility.
Someone who makes things better.
Not because somebody's watching.
Because that's who you are.
And purpose doesn't stay inside you.
Other people feel it.
Someone walks into a room engaged, present, and ready to contribute.
You feel that.
Someone arrives thinking, another day, not my problem.
You feel that too.
Because we create atmosphere everywhere we go.
You bring energy or apathy, care or indifference, calm or chaos.
You are never simply entering an atmosphere.
You are contributing to it.
Purpose creates energy.
And your energy helps create the atmosphere everyone experiences.
You build this through small choices.
You arrive ready.
You greet people properly.
You notice what needs doing.
You help before you're asked.
You do things properly when nobody is watching.
And when there's a problem, instead of asking, whose fault is this?
You ask, what can I do to make this better?
Each choice reinforces something.
This is who I am.
I'm someone who contributes.
I'm someone who serves.
I'm someone who makes things better.
Then you do it again tomorrow, until purpose isn't something you occasionally do.
It's how you show up.
You become the person who brings calm when things are difficult.
Purpose the energy when it's low and cares when something could be better.
That's character.
Will you wake up every morning full of passion?
Of course not.
Purpose isn't pretending everything is wonderful.
And it isn't waiting until you feel motivated.
You don't have to feel purposeful before you act purposefully.
Choose the intention, make the choice, repeat the behavior.
Over time, what you practice becomes part of who you are.
And here's where it gets exciting.
Imagine a whole team arriving with one question.
What am I going to bring today?
One brings enthusiasm.
Another brings excellence.
Another brings creativity.
Someone brings calm.
Someone brings extraordinary care.
And everyone knows, we've got each other's backs.
One person's energy lifts another.
When someone struggles, somebody steps in.
And there's a problem, people solve it together.
Now you're not simply a collection of people doing jobs.
You're creating a culture.
One purposeful person can change their experience of a day.
A team of purposeful people can change an entire environment.
Guests feel it, customers feel it, colleagues feel it.
So before your next working day, don't just ask,
what do I need to do today?
Ask, who am I going to be today?
Complete this sentence.
Today I am someone who brings energy,
excellence, service, calm, joy, care, purpose.
Choose yours, then practice it until you've become it.
Because your work doesn't have to give you purpose.
You bring purpose to your work.
You bring the meaning.
You bring the intention.
You bring the energy.
And together, we create the atmosphere.
I bring my best, you bring your best.
And when a whole team chooses to live and work with purpose,
extraordinary things become possible.
So don't wait for purpose to find you, bring it.
And when we all bring it together,
we can achieve incredible things.
